references.text: The same principle of helping a brother's donkey or ox that has fallen on the road, regardless of personal feelings toward the owner.
Command to take care of a brother's ox or sheep that has gone astray and lead them back to the owner.
Previous verse dealing with returning an enemy's ox or donkey that has gone astray.
Proverbs teach that one should give food and drink to an enemy when he is hungry or thirsty, reflecting the principle of showing kindness to enemies.
Jesus teaches to love your enemies and pray for those who persecute you, which is an extension of the Old Testament principle.
Paul quotes Proverbs and urges giving food and drink to an enemy, in line with the principle of helping an enemy.
Jesus teaches to do good to those who hate you and bless those who curse you.
Clear theological contrast between the authority's role as avenger and the individual's call to show mercy toward enemies.
Deep theological parallel: both require breaking with retaliation by acting toward the hostile one with kindness or non-violence.
Jesus reinforces the principle of Mosaic law: radical kindness toward enemies (turning the other cheek) as a parallel to helping an enemy's donkey.
Clear theological contrast: the requirement for compassion toward an enemy in physical distress versus the requirement for no compassion toward a false prophet.
